options.text: A passing kata or step on a module of the tools wire.
options.why: Right. L2 needs a passing kata or step on a module of the wire, on top of L1.
Wrong. Reading is not evidence on the radar. Explaining a module is what L1 counts.

options.text: A bench run on any wire.
options.why: Wrong. L2 needs a kata or step on a module of the same wire, not a bench on another one.

question: Your radar shows L2 on Tools. Which evidence supports that level?

options.text: Work on those two, taking the next step the radar names for each.
options.why: Right. The radar's next step is built from your evidence, so it names the gap that matters.

options.text: Work on the two you enjoy most.
options.why: Tempting. Enjoyment is not evidence, and it does not show which gap is largest.

options.text: Set both levels higher by hand.
options.why: Wrong. The radar has no control for that. A level comes from your evidence.

question: Your two lowest wires are Permissions and Context. What is the course's advice?

options.text: A passing kata on the loop wire, with the module it came from.
options.why: Right. The line names its module, so the reader can open the evidence.
Wrong. A claim with no module or entry behind it does not belong on the sheet.
